title: Alif Lam Mim: the surah he recited before sleep.
subtitle: Opening letters, and a surah loved at night and Friday dawn
then: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ recited this surah in Fajr on Fridays. Jabir said {reward}he would not sleep until he recited it{/reward} along with Al-Mulk. It opens with letters whose meaning is {idea}known to Allah{/idea}.
now: The last thing you see before sleep is usually a screen. A message, a video, a feed. {reward}His last thing was this surah.{/reward} The three letters are a doorway: stop, listen, then let the night begin.
old: Bedtime is for winding down with my phone.
new: The end of my day can begin with three letters and a pause.
try: Tonight, listen to or read Surah As-Sajdah before you sleep.

title: A Book with no doubt in it, from the Lord of all.
subtitle: Where this revelation comes from
then: The surah introduction says the Makkans called the Prophet's ﷺ words strange inventions. This verse answers first: {idea}there is no doubt whatsoever{/idea} that this Book was sent down from the Lord of all that exists.
now: A video says the Qur'an was edited, borrowed, made up. The comments pile in and you feel unsteady. {idea}Go back to the source{/idea} and read it yourself, slowly, before you let a stranger's doubt settle in you.
old: If people question it loudly enough, maybe it is doubtful.
new: The doubt belongs to the doubter. The Book stands on its own.
try: When a doubt bothers you, read one full page of Qur'an before reading another comment.

title: Not invented. Truth sent to a people with no warner.
subtitle: Why the message came
then: The idol worshippers said the Prophet ﷺ {trap}made it up himself{/trap}. Allah answered: it is the truth from your Lord, sent to warn a people to whom no warner had come, {reward}so they might be guided{/reward}.
now: Your friend never heard the message properly. Only headlines and stereotypes. {reward}The warning was always meant to guide{/reward}, not to shame. You might be the first person who explains it to them gently.
old: A warning is something meant to scare me.
new: The warning came out of care, so people could find their way.
try: Answer one honest question about Islam from a friend, gently and without debate.

title: He created it all. No protector or intercessor but Him.
subtitle: Will you not remember?
then: Ibn Kathir says only He is in control of all affairs. {idea}There is no intercessor except one He permits.{/idea} The question will you not remember is addressed to those who {trap}trusted in others besides Him{/trap}.
now: You need a favour, so you think of who you know. The cousin at the council, the friend in HR. {idea}None of them is a protector without Him.{/idea} Ask Him first, then knock on doors.
old: Getting through life is about knowing the right people.
new: My real protector is Allah, and people only help by His permission.
try: Before asking anyone for help today, ask Allah for it in a short dua.

title: He sends the command down, and it rises back to Him.
subtitle: A Day measured as a thousand of your years
then: Ibn Kathir says His command comes down from above the heavens to {idea}the furthest boundary of the earth{/idea}. Deeds are raised up to Him. The angels cover vast distances {idea}in the blink of an eye{/idea}.
now: Your deadline is Friday and the whole week revolves around it. You check the clock a hundred times. {idea}Your deeds today rise to Him{/idea}, and to Him a thousand years is a Day. What matters is what goes up.
old: My schedule is the biggest clock in my life.
new: His command shapes everything, and my deeds rise to Him each day.
try: At the end of today, think of one deed you would be glad to have raised to Allah.

title: He knows the hidden and the seen. Mighty, and merciful.
subtitle: Might combined with mercy

row.title: the witnessed
sub: what is in front of you

then: Ibn Kathir says He sees all deeds, major and minor. {idea}He is Almighty in His mercy and Most Merciful in His might.{/idea} This is perfection: {reward}merciful without any hint of weakness{/reward}.
now: You know a manager who is strong but cold, and another who is kind but lets everything slide. {reward}Allah is not either of those.{/reward} His strength never stops being mercy, and His mercy never becomes weakness.
old: Power and kindness pull in opposite directions.
new: In Allah, might and mercy are whole together.
try: Be firm about one thing today and kind in how you say it.

title: He made everything well, and began man from clay.
subtitle: From the heavens to the human
then: Zayd bin Aslam said it means {idea}He created everything well and in a goodly fashion{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes that after the heavens and earth, Allah turns to man, starting with {idea}Adam, created from clay{/idea}.
now: The mirror in the morning. The photo you untag. The voice in your head listing what is wrong with you. {idea}The One who made everything well made you too.{/idea} Start from there.
old: There is so much wrong with how I am made.
new: Allah made everything well, and that includes me.
try: Thank Allah today for one part of your body you usually criticise.

title: Every one of us began as a humble drop.
subtitle: Where your story started
then: Ibn Kathir says after Adam, his children {idea}reproduce from a drop{/idea}. The Makkans doubted they could be created again. The surah points them to how they were made the first time.
now: The CEO in the corner office, the cleaner in the corridor, you in between. {idea}All began the same way.{/idea} It is hard to look down on anyone once you remember that.
old: Some people are simply made of better stuff.
new: Every human began from the same humble drop.
try: Greet someone today with the same warmth you would show someone important.

title: Hearing, sight, a heart that understands, and so little thanks.
subtitle: The gifts that make you human
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah shaped Adam, breathed in the soul, and gave {reward}hearing, sight and reason{/reward}. Yet little thanks is given. {idea}The truly blessed one uses them to worship and obey his Lord.{/idea}
now: Your ears took in two hours of podcasts today. Your eyes scrolled a few thousand posts. Your mind worried about a meeting. {reward}Three huge gifts{/reward}, and how much of them went to Allah?
old: My senses are just how my body works.
new: Hearing, sight and thought are gifts to be used for my Lord.
try: Give your ears ten minutes of Qur'an today in place of other audio.

title: Lost in the earth, then made new? Easy for Him.
subtitle: The doubt about resurrection
then: Ibn Kathir says the idol worshippers thought resurrection unlikely once bodies had {trap}disintegrated and dispersed{/trap}. By their own feeble abilities it is. But not for {idea}the One who created them from nothing{/idea}.
now: A funeral, the soil going in, and a quiet thought: is that really it? {idea}Measure it by His power, not yours.{/idea} The One who made you from nothing the first time can make you again.
old: Once someone is buried, it is hard to believe they will rise.
new: The One who made me from nothing can easily make me again.
try: Next time you think of someone who has died, make dua for them and for your meeting again.

title: An angel is assigned to you, and then you return.
subtitle: The angel of death and the return to your Lord
then: Ibn Kathir says the angel of death is a specific angel, and he has helpers. After death comes {idea}the return to your Lord{/idea} on the Day of resurrection, {reward}to receive reward{/reward} or punishment.
now: You plan the next five years: the flat, the promotion, the kids' schools. One appointment is not in your calendar, and it is already set. {idea}It is not an ending, it is a return.{/idea}
old: Death is something I will think about when I am old.
new: An angel is already assigned to me, and after him I go home to my Lord.
try: Spend two quiet minutes today thinking about meeting Allah, then pray your next prayer with that in mind.

title: Heads bowed: now we see, send us back.
subtitle: Certainty that arrives too late
then: Ibn Kathir describes the deniers standing before Allah {trap}with heads bowed in shame{/trap}, asking to be sent back. But Allah knows that if they were returned, {trap}they would behave as before{/trap}.
now: Every one of us has said: if I could go back, I would do it differently. The exam, the argument, the years with a parent. {reward}You are still in the go back part.{/reward} Today is the chance they ask for.
old: There will be time later to get serious.
new: The chance others will beg for is the day I am living now.
try: Do one good deed today that you would wish you had done if it were your last day.

title: He could have forced guidance on every soul. He did not.
subtitle: Guidance is offered, and the choice is real

row.title: it does not matter what I choose

then: Ibn Kathir links this to 10:99: had your Lord willed, {idea}everyone on earth would have believed{/idea}. But His Word took effect, and the abode of those who chose denial is Hell. He adds: {reward}we seek refuge with Allah from that{/reward}.
now: It is easy to say: if Allah wanted me to pray, I would feel like it. {idea}He did not make you a machine.{/idea} The choice to stand up and pray is yours, and it means something because it is yours.
old: If Allah wanted me guided, I would already be.
new: Allah gave me a real choice, and He is waiting for me to use it.
try: Say: I seek refuge with Allah from the Fire, and choose one good act right after.

title: You forgot this Day, so you are treated as forgotten.
subtitle: What forgetting the meeting costs

row.title: forgot the meeting
sub: acted as if it would not come

row.title: a choice to ignore
sub: acting as if it is not real

then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}tried to forget the Day and acted as if they had{/trap}. So they are dealt with as if forgotten, though nothing escapes Allah. He makes the result fit the deed.
now: The reminder you swipe away. The verse you skip because it is uncomfortable. {idea}Forgetting can be a habit we build on purpose.{/idea} The cure is small: keep the Day in mind, a little, every day.
old: Not thinking about the Hereafter is just how busy life works.
new: Forgetting the meeting is a choice, and remembering it is too.
try: Set one daily reminder on your phone that simply says: the meeting with Allah.

title: Reminded by the verses, they fall into prostration.
subtitle: The verse that gives the surah its name
then: The surah is named As-Sajdah after this verse. Ibn Kathir says true believers {idea}listen to the verses and obey them in word and deed{/idea}. They are {reward}not too proud to submit{/reward}, unlike the rebellious who scorn worship.
now: A verse in Taraweeh hits you hard. You feel it in your chest. Then the car park, the traffic, and it is gone. {reward}The believer's response goes all the way down to the floor.{/reward} Sajdah is where a reminder becomes real.
old: Feeling moved by a verse is enough.
new: A reminder is meant to bring me down in sajdah, not just stir me.
try: After your next prayer, stay in one extra sajdah and say subhana rabbiyal a'la slowly.

title: They leave their beds to call their Lord in fear and hope.
subtitle: Night prayer and giving
then: Mujahid and Al-Hasan said this means {idea}voluntary night prayer{/idea}. Ad-Dahhak said Isha and Fajr in congregation. When Mu'adh asked about the gates of goodness, the Prophet ﷺ mentioned {reward}prayer in the depth of the night{/reward} and recited this verse.
now: The alarm for Fajr. The duvet is heavy and warm, and your thumb goes to snooze. {idea}This verse is about that exact moment.{/idea} Getting up is where fear and hope meet.
old: Night prayer is for very pious people, not me.
new: Leaving a warm bed for Allah, even briefly, is the act this verse praises.
try: Tonight, set your alarm ten minutes before Fajr and pray two short rak'ahs.

title: No soul knows the joy kept hidden for them.
subtitle: A hidden reward for hidden deeds
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}because they concealed their good deeds, Allah concealed the reward{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ reported that Allah said He has prepared for His righteous servants {reward}what no eye has seen and no ear has heard{/reward}.
now: You prayed at 4am and told no one. You sent money to a struggling friend with no name on the transfer. {reward}That secret has a secret waiting for it.{/reward} Some things are better kept between you and Allah.
old: If no one knows my good deeds, they barely count.
new: The deeds I hide are the ones Allah answers with a hidden gift.
try: Do one good deed today and tell absolutely no one about it.

title: The believer and the rebel are not equal.
subtitle: Allah's justice does not blur them together
then: Ibn Kathir says that in {idea}His justice and generosity{/idea}, Allah will not judge believers like those who rebelled. Some early scholars said it came about Ali bin Abi Talib and Uqbah bin Abi Mu'ayt.
now: Your honest colleague gets passed over and the one who cuts corners gets promoted. {trap}It feels like it makes no difference.{/trap} {idea}Allah does not score them the same{/idea}, even when the office does.
old: In the end, good and bad people all get the same.
new: Allah's justice keeps them apart, even when the world mixes them up.
try: Keep doing one honest thing at work today, even if it costs you a little.

title: Gardens of Refuge, a welcome for honoured guests.
subtitle: The believers' home
then: Ibn Kathir says the Gardens hold {reward}dwellings, houses and lofty rooms{/reward}. The word used means {reward}something prepared to welcome and honour a guest{/reward}, given for what they used to do.
now: Think of arriving at your grandmother's house after a long trip. The food is ready, the room is made up, she has been waiting. {reward}That is the word used here.{/reward} The believer arrives as an expected guest.
old: If I make it to Paradise, I will just scrape through.
new: Allah welcomes the believer as an honoured guest He has been waiting for.
try: Welcome a guest or visitor today with real care, and think of this verse.

title: No escape from the Fire they used to deny.
subtitle: The end of those who rebelled
then: Ibn Kathir says those who disobeyed Allah will have the Fire as their dwelling, and {trap}every time they try to escape they are returned{/trap}. They are told to taste {trap}what they used to deny{/trap}.
now: You hear a verse like this and want to skip ahead. Stay with it for a moment. {idea}It is meant for you to still have a choice.{/idea} The door of repentance is open today.
old: Verses about the Fire are only for other people.
new: This warning is a mercy that reaches me while I can still turn back.
try: Make sincere tawbah today for one specific thing, and ask Allah to protect you from the Fire.

title: Smaller hardships now, so that they may return.
subtitle: Trials in this world as a wake-up call
then: Ibn Abbas said the nearer punishment means {idea}diseases and problems in this world{/idea}, a test from Allah {idea}so that His servants repent to Him{/idea}. Many early scholars said the same.
now: The car breaks down the week rent is due. A health scare you did not see coming. {idea}It could be a nudge home.{/idea} Before asking why me, ask: is there something I need to turn back from?
old: Bad things in my life are just random.
new: Some hardships are invitations to come back to Allah before it is late.
try: Think of one recent difficulty and ask what it might be calling you back to.

title: Who does more wrong than one reminded who turns away?
subtitle: Turning from a clear reminder

row.title: most misguided, most in need
sub: the one who turns from dhikr

then: Ibn Kathir says no one does more wrong than one who is shown the signs clearly and then {trap}neglects them, as if he does not know them{/trap}. Qatadah said: {idea}beware of turning away from the remembrance of Allah{/idea}.
now: You read the verse about lying, nodded, and lied on the timesheet the same week. {trap}Knowing makes it heavier, not lighter.{/trap} The answer is not to stop reading, but to let the reminder land.
old: If I do not think about the reminder, it does not apply to me.
new: Once I have been reminded, turning away is its own wrong.
try: Pick one reminder you heard this week and act on it today.

title: Musa was given the Book too. This is not new.
subtitle: The same guidance sent before
then: The Makkans called the message strange. Allah reminds them that Musa was given the Book as {idea}guidance for the Children of Israel{/idea}. Qatadah said the line about meeting him refers to {reward}the Night of Isra{/reward}, when the Prophet ﷺ met Musa.
now: Someone at work says your faith is outdated, a set of new rules. {idea}It is the oldest message there is.{/idea} Musa carried it, and the Prophets before and after him. You are in a long line.
old: My faith is something I picked up from my family.
new: I belong to a message carried by Musa and every Prophet.
try: Read the story of Musa in one short passage of the Qur'an this week.

title: Leaders who guide come from patience and certainty.
subtitle: What makes someone worth following
then: Ibn Kathir says leaders arose among them {idea}because they were patient{/idea} in following Allah's commands and believed firmly. When they later twisted the Book, {trap}they lost that position{/trap}. Sufyan said a man cannot be an example unless he shuns the temptation of this world.
now: You are the eldest sibling, the team lead, the parent everyone watches. {idea}People follow what you hold back from{/idea}, not just what you say. Patience is what turns you into someone worth copying.
old: To lead people, I need to be impressive.
new: To lead people well, I need patience and firm faith.
try: Resist one small temptation today, knowing someone younger is watching you.

title: Your Lord will settle every disagreement on that Day.
subtitle: The final judge of what people differed over
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning {idea}what they differed over, in beliefs and actions{/idea}. The disagreements of this life will have a final answer.
now: The comment thread that never ends. The family dispute about an inheritance, five years old now. {idea}Not every argument needs settling by you.{/idea} Some you can leave with the Judge who knows everything.
old: If I do not win this argument, the truth loses.
new: Allah will settle what we differ over. I can speak once and let go.
try: Step out of one online or family argument today without having the last word.

title: They walk through the homes of nations that vanished.
subtitle: Lessons in the ruins

row.title: empty dwellings
sub: as if no one lived there

then: Ibn Kathir says the deniers walked where earlier nations had lived, {trap}yet no trace of them was left{/trap}. In what happened to them, and how the believers were saved, are {idea}signs and important lessons{/idea}.
now: A holiday among ancient ruins. You take selfies by columns where a whole city once lived and planned. {idea}They thought they would last too.{/idea} The question the verse asks is: will you not listen?
old: Old ruins are just tourist spots.
new: Every ruin asks me what I am building that will last.
try: Next time you pass an old building or grave, stop and reflect for one minute.

title: Water driven to dead land, and crops spring up.
subtitle: A sign of kindness and of resurrection
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah explains {reward}His kindness and goodness{/reward} by sending water, from the sky or rivers from the mountains, to land that needs it. He titles it: {idea}the revival of the earth is proof of the resurrection{/idea}.
now: The bread in your lunch, the rice on the table, the milk in your tea. {reward}All of it started as water on dry ground.{/reward} Look at your plate before eating and you are looking at a sign.
old: Food comes from the supermarket.
new: Every meal began with water Allah drove to dead land.
try: Before your next meal, look at the food for a moment and say bismillah slowly.

title: When is this judgement, if you are telling the truth?
subtitle: Mocking the promised Day
then: Ibn Kathir says the disbelievers taunted: all we see of you and your companions is that {trap}you are hiding, afraid and humiliated{/trap}. They asked to hasten it because they thought {trap}it would never happen{/trap}.
now: Someone laughs at your fasting, your prayer, your patience. Where is all this getting you? {idea}The answer has not arrived yet, and that is not the same as never.{/idea} Keep going.
old: If the reward is not visible now, maybe it is not real.
new: Not yet is not never. What Allah promised is on its way.
try: When someone mocks your practice, answer kindly in one line, then carry on.

title: On that Day, late belief will not help.
subtitle: The Day of Judgement leaves no extra time
then: Ibn Kathir says some thought Al-Fath meant the conquest of Makkah. But {idea}on that day the Prophet ﷺ accepted the Islam{/idea} of nearly two thousand people. So it means {trap}Allah's Judgement{/trap}, when belief no longer helps.
now: You keep a list for later: start praying properly, pay back the debt, make up with your sister. {trap}There is a day when later runs out.{/trap} Every item on that list is still possible today.
old: I will believe properly and change once I am sure.
new: Belief only helps while there is still time to live it.
try: Take one item from your later list and do it today.

title: Turn away from them and wait. They are waiting too.
subtitle: Patience while the outcome unfolds
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was told to {idea}turn from them and convey what was revealed{/idea}, and wait for Allah's promise, for He never breaks it. They waited too, plotting. He ends the surah: {reward}sufficient for us is Allah{/reward}.
now: The colleague who keeps waiting for you to slip. The relative who says your new habits will not last. {idea}You do not have to fight every comment.{/idea} Keep doing the right thing and wait for Allah.
old: I need to prove myself to everyone who doubts me.
new: I can keep doing right and leave the outcome to Allah.
try: Say hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil the next time someone's doubt gets to you.
